title: Infinite Sequence Generator with Symbol.iterator
problemStatement: Implement an iterable object `createFibonacciSequence(limit)` that yields Fibonacci numbers up to `limit`. It must support `for...of` iteration and array spreading `[...createFibonacciSequence(50)]`.
interviewTrap: Returning a plain iterator without Symbol.iterator makes an object non-iterable in for...of loops and spread syntax.

testCases.name: Generates Fibonacci sequence up to limit 20
Works seamlessly in standard for...of loop
testCases.testFn: let sum = 0; for (const n of createFibonacciSequence(10)) sum += n; return sum;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Generators are re-entrant state machines. When yield is encountered, the generator's execution context is suspended and pushed out of the call stack. Calling .next() re-attaches the context and resumes evaluation.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Generator State Suspension & Iterable Protocol.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Generator State Suspension & Iterable Protocol is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Returning a plain iterator without Symbol.iterator makes an object non-iterable in for...of loops and spread syntax.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does a generator implement the Iterable protocol via Symbol.iterator?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: A generator object is both an Iterator AND an Iterable. It implements `[Symbol.iterator]() { return this; }`. This allows a generator instance to be passed directly to `for...of` loops, spread operators (`[...gen]`), and destructuring syntax (`const [a, b] = gen`).
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of the dual Iterable/Iterator protocol.

realWorldUseCases.description: Generating mathematical sequences, mock IDs, or infinite series on demand with O(1) memory overhead.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: for (const num of fibonacci()) { if (num > 1000) break; }

howToExplain.opening: An infinite generator produces mathematical sequences lazily, evaluating numbers on demand without allocating arrays in memory.
keyPoints: while(true) with yield pauses execution without blocking the thread.
Consumes O(1) memory regardless of sequence length.
Consumed ergonomically via for...of loops with break conditions.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Generators turn infinite mathematical concepts into practical, memory-safe JavaScript code.
analogies: A water tap: you turn the valve to get a glass of water; the ocean doesn't flood your kitchen all at once.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using spread [...fibonacci()] on an infinite generator.
commonMistakes.why: The spread operator attempts to consume the entire sequence into an array, resulting in an infinite loop and OOM crash.
commonMistakes.correct: Always consume infinite generators with explicit bounds or break conditions.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do BigInt values prevent numeric overflow in Fibonacci generators?
followUpDeepDive.answer: JavaScript numbers are IEEE 754 double-precision floats that lose integer precision past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53 - 1, around Fibonacci #78). Using `0n` and `1n` BigInts allows calculating arbitrary-precision numbers.
